section.title: Activity
section.para: In 2015, the number of wildcats in a national park was 284. It was estimated that the wildcat population increased by 4% each year.

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here are some samples.

list.item: The 284 is the starting population of the wildcats in 2015.
The 1.04 represents that the population grows 4% or 0.04 each year.
The 1.04 comes from 100% of the population + 4% growth = 104% or 1.04.
The \(n\) represents the number of years since 2015. So, in 2016, \(n = 1\) and in 2017, \(n = 2\).

Instead of writing a recursive definition, a researcher for the park writes \(W_n = 284(1.04)^n\), where \(W\) is the projected wildcat population \(n\) years after 2015. Explain where the different factors in her expression came from.

section.para: Work with a partner to discuss and create a table of values to estimate the projected wildcat population over the next 7 years.

list.item: Complete the table when \(n=-2\) on your paper and check your answers.

problem.para: When you have completed the table, then select the solution button to compare your work.

list.item: Use the graphing tool or technology outside the course. Graph the data that represents the population projections for this scenario.

problem.para: When you have finished graphing, select the solution button to compare your work.

div.para: The wildcat population is expected to exceed 500 members in 2030 when they are projected to have 511 wildcats.

list.item: Calculate and enter the year when the wildcat population will exceed 500 members.

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here are some samples:

list.item: This data represents a geometric sequence because the equation has a common ratio of 1.04.
This data represents a geometric sequence because the ratio between consecutive terms in the table is 1.04.
This data represents a geometric sequence because the graph does not depict a line, it is curved a little and does not have a constant slope.
Is the data that represents this scenario an arithmetic or geometric sequence? Explain your reasoning.

section.para: Remember that a recursive formula defines terms using one or more of the previous terms. If you need to calculate the \(100^{th}\) term or the \(500^{th}\) term in a sequence, the recursive formula becomes difficult to use if you do not know the values of the terms near \(n = 100\) or \(n = 500\).

Different definitions can often create the same sequence but are more generalizable. These are called general rules or explicit rules. These formulas can be used to find any term in the sequence and may also be referred to as the rule to find the nth term.

div.title: Geometric Sequence Formulas
div.para:
\(a_n = a_{n-1} \cdot r\),
Where \(a_1\) is the first term, \(n\) is the term you want, and \(r\) is the common ratio.

\(a_n = a_1 (r)^{n-1} \)
Where \(a_1\) is the first term, \(n\) is the term you want, and \(r\) is the common ratio.
